messages:
Marta: Uploaded PR #523 to docs repo — updates to "Audit log export" section. Adds pseudonymization example and clarifies SOC2-friendly retention phrasing. PTAL from legal + docs reviewers
Sana: Nice, thanks. Link to PR?
Marta: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/523 :arrow_right: the main change is a new snippet showing how to redact PII during export, and rewording the TTL vs retention paragraph.
Kevin: Quick skim — looks good. Two nits: 1) the Python snippet uses `user_id` instead of `user_id_hash`, we should show a hashing step. 2) the retention wording still says "we retain for X days by default" — legal prefers "retention TTL" wording.
Marta: Yep, I can add a small hashing line and change that phrasing. Proposed line for Python:
```python
import hashlib
user_id_hash = hashlib.sha256(user_id.encode()).hexdigest()
``` 
Sana: Also add a short curl example for the export CLI. Many customers copy that. Maybe show `jq` masking too.
Noah: From infra side: the export example should call out that exported files are stored encrypted at rest and link to KMS docs. Add a short parenthetical.
Legal: Thanks for tagging. We prefer: "Retention TTL indicates the default retention period for exported audit records; customers may configure longer retention via contract." Avoid "we retain" phrasing. Also, include a line about pseudonymization not being the same as deletion — good to flag.
Marta: Noted. I'll update wording and add the hash snippet + curl example + KMS note. Anyone want to take a quick look at the new text before I merge? I'll wait until EOD PST.
Kevin: I'll take a pass in ~2 hours.
Sana: I'll also review for copy edits.
Marta: Updated PR with changes and added a short curl example:
```bash
# export audit logs with pseudonymized user id
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"start":"2026-03-01","end":"2026-03-15","transform":"pseudonymize(user_id)"}' | jq '.' > export.json
```
Marta: Also added note: "Exports are encrypted at rest (see docs: /security/kms) and subject to customer-configured retention TTLs. Pseudonymization hashes are irreversible for common threat models; they are not a substitute for deletion requests."
Legal: Language LGTM with two tweaks: a) change "irreversible" to "one-way hash"; b) add cross-ref to Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) process. Otherwise okay.
Marta: Done. Pushed fixes and updated the docs-ci checklist. docs-bot: build passed, linkcheck flagged one relative link in /security/kms — fixed.
docs-bot: deploy preview available at https://deploy-preview-523--docs.redwood.ai
Noah: Looks good from infra. Approving.
Kevin: Approved. :thumbsup:
Sana: Approving copy. :sparkles:
Legal: Approving from legal. :white_check_mark:
Marta: Thanks all — merging in 30m unless anyone objects.
